problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=-2.$ Given that the point $P(-2,-6,1)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=\frac{y-x}{\sqrt{x(y+x)}}$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$

feedback.problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=1.$ Given that the point $P(2,1,4)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}={e}^{y-1}+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y-1)$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface with the plane $y=1.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(2,1).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(2,1) & ={e}^{1-1}+2(2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(1-1) \\  & =1+4 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(2,1) & ={f}_{x}(2,1)(x-2) \\ z-4 & =5(x-2) \\ z & =5x-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(2,1,4)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=1 \\ z=5x-6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $y=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨0,1,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=5x-6$ (or $5x-z-6=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨5,0,-1⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨0,1,0⟩\times ⟨5,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-i-5\,k \\  & =⟨-1,0,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $⟨-1,0,-5⟩$ is parallel to the tangent line, then $-⟨-1,0,-5⟩=⟨1,0,5⟩$ is also parallel to it.
